clue.text: Deer on grass, possibly in parks

definitions.note: the definition describes where such plots are typically found rather than naming them directly

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters may be arranged in another order

explanation.surface: A deer grazing on a lawn, as you might see in a public park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the letters of DEER ON GRASS. The definition is loose: it tells you where these beds of blooms are commonly laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal beds of roses are a familiar feature laid out in municipal parks.

clue.text: Spare serving men wait at table

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of soldiers in service
to wait at table is to serve food

explanation.surface: Extra staff are on hand to wait on diners.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps, so 'serving men' are soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare is something kept back for later use, a backup or substitute.

clue.text: Discerning chic

explanation.surface: Someone with a good eye for fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both clever or shrewd and fashionably stylish.

clue.text: Inexperienced band has no place for development

parts.note: green means new and inexperienced
a belt is a band worn round the waist

explanation.surface: A group of novice musicians has nowhere to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is protected open land round a town where building is restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a planning zone of countryside around a city where building is forbidden.

clue.text: Some furniture, a desk etc, suitable for study

indicators.note: some says only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Office furniture such as a desk is good to work at.
explanation.definitionFit: To study a subject, especially at university, is to take it as a course of learning.

clue.text: 26 will ensure agreement among those rowing

definitions.note: the answer to 26 across, a faculty such as sight

indicators.note: among says the agreeing word sits within the crew word

parts.note: an eight is a crew of rowers
yes expresses agreement

explanation.surface: Good sense will make a rowing crew agree.
explanation.walkthrough: '26' refers to the answer of 26 across; vision is one of the five faculties of perception.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the bodily faculties of perception alongside hearing and touch.

clue.text: Clash, but not much

explanation.surface: A minor fight hardly worth mentioning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a brief fight or tussle and a tiny bit or fragment.

clue.text: Huff taken about bond being invalid

definitions.note: used here as a noun, a sick person

indicators.note: taken about says the first word is placed around the second

parts.note: to huff is to puff or pant
a tie is a bond or link

explanation.surface: Someone sulks when a contract is declared void.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Huff' looks like a sulk but means breathe hard, and 'invalid' is a noun (a sick person), not 'void'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person under medical care, an invalid, is someone being treated by a doctor.

clue.text: Against Sunday-opening, they reckon

definitions.note: plural people, matching the plural answer

parts.note: counter means against, opposed

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Opponents of Sunday trading give their opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they reckon' looks like 'they think' but means people who count or calculate.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who tally or calculate figures are people who count.

clue.text: Old partner responsible for stand-off

parts.note: stale means old and no longer fresh
a mate is a partner or companion

explanation.surface: A former spouse caused the deadlock.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock in which neither side can make progress, from the drawn chess position.

clue.text: Nonsense written about very large perch

indicators.note: written about says the first word goes around the second

parts.note: rot is nonsense
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Rubbish has been published about an enormous freshwater fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' tempts as the fish, but it is a bird's resting place.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where birds settle to rest, a perch.

clue.text: Seaman's classification

explanation.surface: The grade assigned to a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an ordinary sailor in the navy and a grading or ranking.

clue.text: Allot the underworld prison quarters

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and his realm
a pen is an enclosure, a prison
S and E are two compass quarters, south and east

explanation.surface: Assign rooms in a jail in hell.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to share out or distribute.

clue.text: Resulted from getting the wind up about petition

indicators.note: about says the first word goes round the second

parts.note: to wind up is to end
to sue is to petition or appeal

explanation.surface: Panic followed a legal appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting the wind up' (being scared) misleads: 'wind up' means finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To have followed as a consequence, resulted.

clue.text: A listening device put in to influence the strong language

indicators.note: put in says the device goes inside the other word

parts.note: to swing is to influence a result
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A bug planted to sway someone's forceful speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listening device' suggests a bug, but it is the human ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Cursing and profanity is coarse or strong language.

clue.text: The least expensive copy in the box

indicators.note: in places the copying word inside the box word

parts.note: a chest is a box
to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: The cheapest reproduction in the packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowest in price, costing least of all.

clue.text: Vigilance of stern eccentric taking drinks outside

indicators.note: outside says the drinks word goes round the rest

parts.note: ales are drinks

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The watchfulness of an odd stern figure who drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges STERN into RTNES, which goes inside ALES.
explanation.definitionFit: Watchfulness and readiness to respond, vigilance.

clue.text: He believes a lot can't be changed

definitions.text: He believes a lot can't be changed

parts.words: He believes a lot can't be changed
parts.note: a lot here is one's fate or destiny, which this kind of person accepts as fixed

explanation.surface: A man who thinks much is beyond change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' reads as 'many things' but means one's lot in life, one's destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who thinks all events are predetermined and destiny is fixed.

clue.text: Final net value may be worked out

indicators.note: worked out suggests the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: The bottom line figure may need calculating.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventual means ultimately happening, final.

clue.text: Passed over no longer, a large number applied

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
used means applied

explanation.surface: No longer ignored, many were put to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Excused means let off or exempted, passed over.

clue.text: Proficient in the main, but over-sedulous

indicators.note: in the main means mostly, so most of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Skilled at sea, but too painstaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' suggests the sea, but the phrase means 'mostly': most of 'over-sedulous' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be versed is to be skilled and knowledgeable.

clue.text: Tardy as can be, though seen before sunrise

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters can form another word

explanation.surface: Someone as late as possible yet up before dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The morning star, the planet Venus visible at dawn.

clue.text: Welsh knitwear?

parts.note: a knitted jacket that shares its name with a town in Wales

explanation.surface: A garment from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: The town in west Wales and the buttoned woollen jacket share a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted buttoned jumper, named after the Earl, is also a town in Wales.

clue.text: Setting a writer up in it would be pointless

indicators.note: in places the reversed writer inside the other word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read upwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing tool

explanation.surface: Placing an author in it would be futile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PEN into NEP, which goes inside IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy and ineffective, pointless.

clue.text: Being short, top-drawer politician is in beastly accommodation

indicators.note: is in places the politician inside the pig pen

parts.note: a sty is a pig pen
U means upper class, top-drawer
MP is a member of parliament

explanation.surface: An upper-class politician is short and living in a pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: Short and thick, squat.

clue.text: Note a hard worker is indicated

parts.note: me is a variant spelling of mi in sol-fa
an ant is a hard worker

explanation.surface: A musical note means someone diligent is pointed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Meant means signified or indicated.

clue.text: The tiresome person parking badly

parts.note: ill means badly

explanation.surface: An annoying driver who parks poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pill is a bore, a tiresome person.

clue.text: Divine substance

explanation.surface: Holy matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to sense, perceive; substance is meaning or gist.

clue.text: The migrant worker's object in a rent arrangement

parts.note: it is a pronoun for an object

indicators.note: arrangement says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The aim of a migrant labourer in a rental deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges IN A RENT into INERANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller who moves from place to place to work.

clue.text: It's a better system of course

definitions.text: It's a better system of course

parts.words: It's a better system of course
parts.note: a better here is a punter who bets, and the course is a racecourse

explanation.surface: This is naturally an improved method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' means one who bets, and 'course' is a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine at the races that pools bets and calculates the payouts.
